question.problem:
Suppose that $f(x,y)$ is a differentiable function such that

$$
f(-2,0)=-3,\,{f}_{x}(-2,0)=1,\,{f}_{y}(-2,0)=0.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(-2,0),$ estimate the value of $f(-1.99,0.01).$
question.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y)≈f(a,b)+∇f(a,b)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(-2,0)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ≈f(-2,0)+∇f(-2,0)\cdot ⟨x-(-2),y-0⟩ \\  & =f(-2,0)+⟨{f}_{x}(-2,0),{f}_{y}(-2,0)⟩\cdot ⟨x+2,y⟩ \\  & =-3+⟨1,0⟩\cdot ⟨x+2,y⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(-1.99,0.01)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=-1.99$ and $y=0.01,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1.99,0.01) & ≈-3+⟨1,0⟩\cdot ⟨-1.99+2,0.01⟩ \\  & =-3+⟨1,0⟩\cdot ⟨0.01,0.01⟩ \\  & =-3+1(0.01)+0(0.01) \\  & =-3+0.01+0 \\  & =-2.99\end{aligned}
$$
